contractSource: Description: "Calculate required insulation thickness for pipes, walls, and surfaces using thermal conductivity..." Modes: Target surface temperature, Max heat loss, Target U-value.
groundTruth: Steady state through a flat layer: heat conducted through the insulation k·(Tf − Ts)/t equals heat leaving the surface h·(Ts − Ta). So t = k·(Tf − Ts) / (h·(Ts − Ta)). For still indoor air the combined surface coefficient h is about 8–12 W/m²·K (convection + radiation). For a U-value target (surface resistances neglected) t = k / U.

cases.note: The surface-temperature method on a hot surface.
cases.derivation: k = 0.04 W/m·K, fluid 150 °C, target surface 40 °C, ambient 25 °C. t = 0.04 × (150 − 40) / (h × (40 − 25)) = 4.4 / (15h) m. With h = 12 → 24.4 mm; h = 10 → 29.3 mm; h = 8 → 36.7 mm. 30 ± 7 mm covers the band. A result near 293 mm would mean h was left out (h = 1).

cases.note: The U-value method, which should be right.
